chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said in one of his sermons:

'O people! Know that he is not possessed of intellect who becomes agitated by false words spoken about him, nor is he possessed of wisdom who is pleased with the eulogies of the ignorant directed at him.
The people are the offspring of what they excel in, and the worth of every person is what he excels in.
Therefore, speak about knowledge — your worth will become manifest.'

key_terms.بِحَكِيمٍ: possessed of hikmah (wisdom) — a person of sound and balanced judgment
key_terms.بِعَاقِلٍ: possessed of 'aql (intellect/reason) — one who governs himself by reason rather than emotion
key_terms.قَدْرُ: worth, rank, intrinsic measure — the true value of a person

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (AS) say about the worth of a person and the marks of true intellect in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this sermon recorded in al-Kafi, Imam Ali (AS) sets out two hallmarks of genuine intellect and wisdom: remaining unmoved by slander, and being indifferent to the praise of the ignorant. He then articulates the celebrated maxim that a person's true worth is measured by the knowledge and skill they master, and exhorts his audience to demonstrate that worth through discourse on knowledge.
